h: Mill Hill, Museums and Green Belt Views
p: Belmont Children's Farm sits on the leafy fringes around Mill Hill in the London Borough of Barnet, where the city frays into fields and hedgerows. It feels a world away from central London, yet you're still within the capital, which makes it a smart pick for families who want a countryside fix without the long drive out to the shires.

Small farms like this are perfect for a toddler's first proper animal encounter. Let them watch from a distance first, then build up to a closer look once they're comfortable. Hold little hands near the fences, follow any signs about feeding and touching, and wash hands well afterwards, especially before snacks. A bit of patience at the pens often pays off when a curious nose comes over to investigate. Early in the day tends to be calmer if you've got a little one who's sensitive to crowds.

North London has plenty of easy add-ons. The RAF Museum at Hendon, a short drive away, is packed with historic aircraft, from early biplanes to famous wartime fighters and bombers, and kids who love planes will be in their element. It's a brilliant indoor option if the weather turns after your farm visit. Mill Hill itself has a village feel along The Ridgeway and around Mill Hill Broadway, with cafés for a refuel, and the surrounding green belt has footpaths for a stroll in the fields. Pair the farm in the morning with the planes in the afternoon and you've got a day that suits animal lovers and aviation fans alike.
